kings2.18.p1.b1.text: In the third year of the reign of Hoshea son of Elah over Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz became king of Judah. He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. … And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father David had done.

kings2.18.p1.b2.text: He removed the high places, shattered the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah poles.

kings2.18.p1.b3.text: He also demolished the bronze snake called Nehushtan that Moses had made, for up to that time the Israelites had burned incense to it.

kings2.18.p1.b4.text: Hezekiah trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel. No king of Judah was like him, either before him or after him.

kings2.18.p2.b1.text: And the LORD was with Hezekiah, and he prospered wherever he went. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and refused to serve him.

kings2.18.p2.b2.text: He defeated the Philistines as far as Gaza and its borders, from watchtower to fortified city.

kings2.18.p2.b3.text: In the fourth year of Hezekiah’s reign, … Shalmaneser king of Assyria marched against Samaria and besieged it. And at the end of three years, the Assyrians captured it.

kings2.18.p2.b4.text: This happened because they did not listen to the voice of the LORD their God, but violated His covenant—all that Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded—and would neither listen nor obey.

kings2.18.p3.b1.text: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.

kings2.18.p3.b2.text: So Hezekiah king of Judah sent word to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, “I have done wrong; withdraw from me, and I will pay whatever you demand from me.” And the king of Assyria exacted from Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.

kings2.18.p3.b3.text: Hezekiah gave him all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the royal palace.

kings2.18.p3.b4.text: At that time Hezekiah stripped the gold with which he had plated the doors and doorposts of the temple of the LORD, and he gave it to the king of Assyria.

kings2.18.p4.b1.text: … The king of Assyria sent the Tartan, the Rabsaris, and the Rabshakeh, along with a great army, from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. … They advanced up to Jerusalem and stationed themselves by the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field.

kings2.18.p4.b2.text: Then they called for the king; and Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebnah the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, went out to them.

kings2.18.p5.b1.text: This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is the basis of this confidence of yours? … In whom are you now trusting, that you have rebelled against me?

kings2.18.p5.b2.text: Look now, you are trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff that will pierce the hand of anyone who leans on it.

kings2.18.p5.b3.text: But if you say to me, ‘We trust in the LORD our God,’ is He not the One whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed …?

kings2.18.p6.b1.text: Now, therefore, make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you two thousand horses—if you can put riders on them!

kings2.18.p6.b2.text: For how can you repel a single officer among the least of my master’s servants when you depend on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?

kings2.18.p6.b3.text: So now, was it apart from the LORD that I have come up against this place to destroy it? The LORD Himself said to me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it.’”

kings2.18.p7.b1.text: Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since we understand it. Do not speak with us in Hebrew in the hearing of the people on the wall.

kings2.18.p7.b2.text: Has my master sent me to speak these words only to you and your master, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are destined with you to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?

kings2.18.p8.b1.text: Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria! This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you; he cannot deliver you from my hand.

kings2.18.p8.b2.text: Do not let Hezekiah persuade you to trust in the LORD when he says, ‘The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.’

kings2.18.p8.b3.text: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then every one of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and drink water from his own cistern …

kings2.18.p8.b4.text: Until I come and take you away to a land like your own … so that you may live and not die. But do not listen to Hezekiah, for he misleads you when he says, ‘The LORD will deliver us.’

kings2.18.p9.b1.text: Has the god of any nation ever delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria? … How then can the LORD deliver Jerusalem from my hand?

kings2.18.p9.b2.text: But the people remained silent and did not answer a word, for Hezekiah had commanded, “Do not answer him.”

kings2.18.p9.b3.text: Then Hilkiah’s son Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Asaph’s son Joah the recorder … with their clothes torn …

kings2.18.p9.b4.text: … came to Hezekiah … and they relayed to him the words of the Rabshakeh.
